clue.text: Dare a big letter to get funds for business

parts.note: to dare is to take a chance, to risk
an upper-case letter is a capital

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gamble on writing a grand letter to raise money for a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture money put into a business at the investor's own hazard is the standard financial term here.

clue.text: Bad weather I left: at speed?

indicators.note: left in the sense of departed, so the letter I goes out of the word

parts.note: rain is the classic bad weather

explanation.surface: A traveller, fed up with the downpour, quit and hurried off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' means take the I away from RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at speed is what one did if one sprinted; the question mark flags the loose past-tense paraphrase.

clue.text: Black bishop goes in exchange

indicators.note: the bishop's letter goes into the other word, so a container

parts.note: a sale is an exchange of goods for money
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess move: the dark bishop is traded off.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'Black bishop' look like one piece; 'Black' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for the colour black.

clue.text: Bluish fish that's deadly

parts.note: cyan is a greenish-blue colour
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A blue-tinted fish turns out to be poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound is a notorious fast-acting poison, so it is a thing that kills.

clue.text: Repaying change collected originally as tribute

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in repaying plus the extra one
originally means take just the opening letter of collected

explanation.surface: Money collected to pay someone back is presented as a tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives C from 'collected', which joins REPAYING before 'change' rearranges all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or text of high praise, a tribute to someone.

clue.text: Run, carrying a pack

indicators.note: the running word carries the a inside it, making a container

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: Jog along with a backpack on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' looks like a rucksack but means a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-tellers use a special deck of cards, so it is a pack in the card sense.

clue.text: Two means of support keep a man newly-enriched?

indicators.note: the two supports keep the a between them, holding it inside

parts.note: a leg supports a body or table
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Two props hold up a man who has just come into money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'newly-enriched' as a description of a man; the question mark marks it as a playful definition of an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left something in a will has suddenly been made richer by the bequest.

clue.text: Fool's lousy production

definitions.meaning: what a louse produces: its egg

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dimwit in British slang and the egg of a louse, which is literally lousy output.

clue.text: I snack with men at work Chalky and Shorty, for instance

indicators.note: the letters are put to work and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone snacks among workmates known as Chalky and Shorty.
explanation.walkthrough: Chalky (traditionally given to anyone called White) and Shorty are typical British informal names for workmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal names given to people in place of their real ones, so they are examples.

clue.text: Ridiculous to name a ship Revolutionary

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the words are made absurd, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: It would be silly to christen a vessel with a radical's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like an adjective but is the definition: the writer of Common Sense who backed the American and French revolutions.
explanation.definitionFit: The English-born author of Common Sense and Rights of Man was a leading radical of the American Revolution.

clue.text: Head introduces Rilke, a simple task

indicators.note: the head word comes first and introduces the poet's name after it

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
the poet Rainer Maria Rilke

explanation.surface: A leader presents the German poet Rilke to an audience as easy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needing no thought at all is an easy job, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Cold-blooded type to travel round City to finish off bank

indicators.note: the travelling word goes round the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to go is to travel
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: finish off means take the final letter of bank

explanation.surface: A reptile sets off around the City to close down a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lizard, and reptiles are cold-blooded animals.

clue.text: Applying to have royal audience

definitions.meaning: trying to obtain, as when applying for a post
to be received by the monarch, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Applying for something means trying to get it, the same as looking for it.

clue.text: Overrule judges in match venue

parts.note: to squash a decision is to overrule it
a court is a body of judges

explanation.surface: Judges overturn a ruling at the sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed room where games of squash rackets are played, so a place for matches.

clue.text: Busy about province, a queen

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the busy phrase round, reading it backwards

parts.note: at it means busy, hard at work
NI is Northern Ireland, the province

explanation.surface: A bustling queen travels round her province.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream, wife of Oberon.

clue.text: Pop in here? No, his brother

definitions.meaning: pop means pawn, and a pawnbroker is slang for this relative
pop as a father: his brother is the relative

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pawnbroker, where you pop things, and also the brother of one's father.

clue.text: Lace worker in unheated housing

indicators.note: the cold word houses the insect inside it

parts.note: an unheated room is chilly
a worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A lacemaker toils in a cold, unheated workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate bobbin lace named after the French town where it was made.

clue.text: Street plan of Mafeking once?

parts.note: a map of a town during its famous siege-lifting in the Boer War, also a map showing hills and valleys

explanation.surface: An old map of the South African town of Mafeking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Relief of Mafeking (1900) ended a famous Boer War siege; the term also names a map showing heights in raised form.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing terrain heights, punned with the lifting of the siege of Mafeking.

clue.text: The end of the harvest proved back-breaking

definitions.text: The end of the harvest proved back-breaking

parts.words: The end of the harvest proved back-breaking
parts.note: the final stalk gathered is the one that broke the camel's back in the proverb

explanation.surface: The final stage of reaping turned out to be exhausting work.
explanation.definitionFit: The final burden that makes something unbearable, from the proverbial straw that broke the camel's back.

clue.text: Rebel slave wanting to fight us receiving whip on back

parts.note: to spar is to fight

indicators.note: on back tells us to read the whip word backwards

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
us taken as written, receiving the turned whip just in front of it

explanation.surface: A rebellious slave refuses to fight on with a whip at his back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator who led a slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Discretion about one useless historian

indicators.note: the discretion word goes about the numeral, holding it

parts.note: tact is discretion
I is the Roman numeral one
US is short for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: A tactful man is little help as a chronicler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman historian who wrote the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: After soups regularly welcome cold food

indicators.note: the greeting comes after the soup letters
regularly means take every other letter of soups

parts.note: hi is a welcome greeting

explanation.surface: Once the soup course is done, raw fish is served to welcome guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese dish of rice and raw fish is served cold.

clue.text: Completely upset by terrible threats

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of threats are put into a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply disturbed by awful threats.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter someone is to devastate them emotionally, upsetting them entirely.

clue.text: Skin heads of city laid into sweet girl

indicators.note: the picked letters go into the girl word

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive girl

indicators.note: heads of means the opening letters of city and laid

explanation.surface: Bosses from the city attacked a pretty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' reads as attacked, but 'laid' is a source of a letter and 'into' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the layer of skin at the base of a fingernail.

clue.text: Seem mercenary, fencing crop

indicators.note: fencing means the two words enclose the answer between them

explanation.surface: A farmer appears greedy, putting up fences around his harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient type of wheat grown as a cereal crop.

clue.text: Big beast hits back, showing wit

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole run of letters in reverse

parts.note: the elk is a big deer
raps are hits

explanation.surface: A large animal strikes back, displaying a sharp mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ELK + RAPS as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkle is liveliness and brilliance in conversation, a kind of wit.

clue.text: After wine concoction, heartily love Stalinist

indicators.note: the middle letters follow the wine word

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and cassis

indicators.note: heartily means take the heart, the middle letters, of love

explanation.surface: After a mixed drink, someone warmly professes love for Stalin's man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Kirov was a Soviet leader loyal to Stalin, assassinated in 1934.

clue.text: Military team circles lake in the dark

indicators.note: the unit circles the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a unit is a military group

explanation.surface: Soldiers surround a lake at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so in darkness.

clue.text: Intend to return, accepting speaker's pauses

indicators.note: the turned word accepts the speaker inside it
return tells us to read the intending word backwards

parts.note: to aim is to intend
an orator is a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone plans to come back after hearing a speaker's halting delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns AIM into MIA, which takes in ORATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria is the plural of moratorium, a temporary halt or suspension.

clue.text: Suggesting twelve months in Scottish town?

definitions.text: Suggesting twelve months in Scottish town?

parts.words: Suggesting twelve months in Scottish town?
parts.note: the town's name looks like the letter A followed by the short form of year

explanation.surface: A year spent in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayrshire's county town; its name reads as A YR, 'a year'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the west coast of Scotland whose written name resembles a period of a year.

clue.text: Scottish river the Irish drink?

indicators.note: the Irish, in stage-Irish speech, say the drink's name to rhyme with day

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Is the Scots river what the Irish drink?
explanation.walkthrough: In a traditional Irish accent the drink is said 'tay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's longest river, flowing through Perth to Dundee.

clue.text: Second eight runs into chap in water — it gives the fixer a turn

definitions.text: it gives the fixer a turn

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the swimmer word

parts.note: a diver is a person in water
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A second rowing eight runs into a swimmer, giving the repairman a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it gives the fixer a turn' is cryptic: the tool turns a screw, a fixer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand tool rotates screws, which are fixings, so it turns the fixer.
